references.text: Psalm 23:1 reminds us that the Lord is our shepherd, and we shall not lack anything, which echoes the trust in God's provision that Jesus encourages in Matthew 6:31.
Proverbs 3:5 urges us to trust in the Lord with all our heart and not lean on our own understanding, which resonates with the call not to worry found in Matthew 6:31.
In 1 Kings 17:11-16, God provides for the widow of Zarephath through Elijah, illustrating God's ability to provide, as Jesus refers to in Matthew 6:31.
In Matthew 10:9-10, Jesus instructs his disciples not to acquire gold, silver, or copper for their money belts, demonstrating trust in God's provision, similar to what is taught in Matthew 6:31.
Luke 12:22-31 contains parallel teaching from Jesus about not worrying over life's necessities, which directly corresponds with Matthew 6:31.

Hebrews 13:5 encourages us to keep our lives free from the love of money and be content with what we have, for God has said he will never leave us, reflecting the trust in God's provision found in Matthew 6:31.
